market_brief: Relief is broadening into the US open: S&P futures are up about 2.9% and Nasdaq 100 about 3.6% after Friday's correction close (S&P 6,910, -3.7%; SOX -10.7%; VIX 35.9), led by Nvidia (~+9% pre-market) after Trump urged its board to rehire Jensen Huang, while CrowdStrike's $43.9bn Zscaler bid sank CRWD ~9%. India did not share the bounce: after the 07:46 snapshot (Nifty -1.3%), Nifty closed -1.75% at 25,350 and Bank Nifty -3.2%, with markets shut Tuesday. Havens are unwinding last week's liquidation, with gold up about 3% to ~$3,625 and silver ~+3.7%, while Brent slipped about 3% toward $89.5 as freight premia ease despite Gulf attacks. Rates remain the swing factor: Treasury yields are edging up from 4.91% on the 10Y, December hike odds sit near 91-92%, and Williams speaks today; DXY ~103.6, BTC ~$61.4k.
ai_brief: Zhipu's GLM-5.4 is the notable launch, a looped-layer model claiming big-model quality at lower cost, while Ant open-sourced a 560B medical model. Security and distribution are tightening after the hosting-leak findings, with OpenAI now vetting gateway resellers. Agents keep moving into real actions (AWS DevOps Agent writes, Architect Labs' AI-designed CPU claim), and Meta's emissions jump highlights AI's power bill.

items.headline: Nvidia jumps about 9% pre-market after Trump urges the board to rehire Jensen Huang
items.summary: Trump posted that he hopes Nvidia's board rehires Huang, and Bessent softened his stance, saying Huang is now 'on the outside'. The stock is rebounding from a 14% Friday drop to $125.53; the board has said it does not intend to reinstate him, and Bessent's Nov 25 deadline on chip-diversion questions still stands.

items.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in a $43.9bn all-stock deal
items.summary: The 1.135-share exchange ratio implies about $260 per Zscaler share, a ~34% premium; CrowdStrike fell about 9% pre-market and Zscaler rose about 13%. The companies target ~$1bn revenue synergies and $500m cost savings, with closing expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028.

items.headline: Update: US futures extend the rebound to about 3% ahead of a holiday-shortened week
items.summary: S&P 500 futures rose about 2.9% to ~7,136 and Nasdaq 100 futures about 3.6%, extending the Sunday-night bounce after Friday's correction close at 6,910. Friday's chip losers led, after Nvidia, Arm and Micron each fell about 14%.

items.headline: Update: India reverses its early gain and closes sharply lower; Sensex down 1,484 points
items.summary: Nifty fell 1.75% to 25,349.65 and Sensex 1.77% to 82,435.99, with Bank Nifty down about 3.2% and metals about 3.7%, while IT gained roughly 2%. Tata Steel, Axis Bank and HDFC Bank led losses; markets are shut Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti.

items.headline: Eurozone flash PMI steady at 51.7 as services miss; UK composite slips to 52.3
items.summary: Eurozone services came in at 51.2 versus 51.8 expected, with Germany accelerating and France contracting at its fastest pace in six months. European stocks still rebounded on broad short covering.

items.headline: Treasury yields climb as risk rebounds; NY Fed's Williams speaks today
items.summary: Yields rose from Friday's lows (10Y around 4.95% midday in Europe vs 4.91% Friday close) as equity futures recovered. Williams said last week further hikes are likely but nothing dramatic is needed, so markets watch his tone after the rout.

items.headline: Prediction markets: December Fed hike odds near 91%; Kalshi odds of Huang's return rise to 16%
items.summary: Polymarket put a Dec 9 hike at about 91%, down from 98% on Nov 12, with bond pricing near 92%. Separately, Kalshi traders lifted the probability of Huang returning as Nvidia CEO to 16% from under 10% last week, per Yahoo Finance.

items.headline: Bill Ackman warns a December Fed hike could tip the US into recession
items.summary: The Pershing Square founder reportedly argued that tightening into the tech sell-off risks a downturn, adding to Bessent's weekend warning against overtightening.

items.headline: Oil slips despite weekend Gulf shipping attacks as freight premia ease
items.summary: January Brent traded near $90.9 and WTI near $82 early in New York after UKMTO reported multiple attacks near Hormuz and an unconfirmed Houthi claim on a Saudi refinery. Goldman notes Atlantic crude freight is down 60-70% from its October peak; COP31 ended without a deal and OPEC+ meets Nov 29.

items.headline: Gold and silver extend the rebound; MCX gold up 2.5%
items.summary: Spot gold traded around $3,610-3,625, up roughly 2.5-3% after last week's liquidity-driven selling, and silver rose over 3%. In India, December MCX gold settled near Rs 1,24,818 per 10g.

items.headline: Bitcoin steadies near $61.5k after a weekend dip to a two-year low of $55,130
items.summary: Spot bitcoin ETFs have lost nearly $3bn in November and a fear-and-greed gauge sits at 9, signalling extreme fear. Analysts cite $62-65k as resistance and $55-56k as support.

items.headline: Texas Pacific Land to buy EagleRock in a ~$3.0bn all-stock deal
items.summary: EagleRock holders get 0.0831 new TPL shares each, about $23.56 per share, ending up with ~14% of the combined company. TPL also raised its buyback authorisation to $500m; closing is expected in 1H 2027.

items.headline: Dell and HPE reportedly sought AI server price increases of up to 45% after deals were signed
items.summary: The report adds to concerns about AI hardware costs a day before Dell's earnings; HPE reports after Monday's close.

items.headline: Week ahead: Dell, HP, Best Buy Tuesday; Deere, PCE and GDP Wednesday; US closed Thursday
items.summary: 38 companies worth $2bn or more report this week, 23 of them on Tuesday. US markets shut for Thanksgiving on Nov 26 and close early on Nov 27; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 and the Fed decides Dec 9.

items.headline: Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, its first Loop Transformer flagship
items.summary: GLM-5.4 runs 28 GLM-5 layers twice and adds vision; it is live for GLM Coding Plan, ZCode and Z.ai Chat, with API and open weights promised after safety work. Z.ai claims quality comparable to 2-3T-parameter models but has not yet published benchmarks.

items.headline: OpenAI now requires approval for router and gateway resellers of its models
items.summary: The policy, effective Nov 20, follows reports of prompt leaks among inference hosts; OpenRouter separately dropped three providers and pulled zero-retention status from 125 endpoints.

items.headline: Startup says AI agents designed a CPU with 4.6x better performance per watt in simulation
items.summary: Architect Labs' 'Frostbite' design showed 4.59x perf/watt across 25 workloads in pre-silicon simulation; no physical chip exists yet, so the claim is unverified.

items.headline: Ant releases an open-weight medical model with 560B total parameters
items.summary: LingSante-3.1-flash uses a mixture-of-experts design with 25B active parameters, aimed at healthcare tasks.

items.headline: OpenAI publishes MedChemBench; GPT-6.2 Astra scores 84.5%
items.summary: The benchmark has 99 medicinal-chemistry problems; OpenAI reports its top model's score at the highest reasoning-effort setting.

items.headline: AWS DevOps Agent can now take write actions across GitHub, GitLab, ServiceNow and PagerDuty
items.summary: Actions are customer-directed, moving the agent beyond diagnosis into making changes across common DevOps tools.

items.headline: Update: Bessent says Trump and Xi discussed keeping humans in charge of major military AI decisions
items.summary: This adds detail to weekend reports that Washington and Beijing are exploring joint AI safeguards; no formal agreement has been announced.

items.headline: Meta re-evaluates its 2030 net-zero goal as AI build-out lifts emissions about 40%
items.summary: Reported emissions rose from 15.6m to over 21.7m tonnes CO2e between 2024 and 2025. SpaceX's $74bn AI data-centre plans face similar power-cost questions.

items.headline: Signal blocks OS-level AI assistants from reading chats via screenshots by default
items.summary: New screen-capture protections on iOS and Android aim to keep built-in mobile assistants out of private messages.

items.headline: Nothing teases a screenless AI-native device for a December 8 unveiling
items.summary: The consumer-hardware maker joins the wave of agent-first gadgets; details have not been released.
